slides.title: Revenge trading: how one loss becomes five.
slides.text: It's not a strategy problem. It's a **rules** problem.

points.t: "I just need to get it back."
A loss hurts more than an equal win feels good.
You stop trading setups and start trading your P&L.

points.b: Set the limit in your platform
points.t: Many platforms and prop firms can lock you out at a loss.

points.b: Write the reason before every entry
points.t: If you can't, it's probably revenge.
Count how much came after the first loss.

slides.title: The first loss is a cost. The next five are a choice.
slides.text: Decide your stop-trading rules before the open, and make them hard to break.

post.instagram:
Re-entering right after a stop, doubling the size, moving the stop: that's revenge trading. Rules that stop it: a break after 2 losses in a row, a daily loss limit that ends the day, same or smaller size after a loss, and new trades only from your plan.

Save this for later and follow @calmedgeofficial for one trading concept a day.

Educational content. Not financial advice; trading involves risk of loss.
